title: [Chapitre] VIII. Analysis situs (quatrième mouture) : notes manuscrites (26/06-04/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is the 'quatrième mouture' of Analysis situs (1986). Grothendieck works with a set M of 'pieces' (cells or strata of a tame or combinatorial space) containing a subset L of 'elementary' pieces. Each X in M has an 'ombre' omb°(X), a subset of L (its shadow). He studies the ordered sets Σ_M and Σ_L of '(interior) supports', i.e. sets of the form cosupp°(A).

Previous page. He defines two maps:
- Σ_M → Σ_L, S ↦ S ∩ L;
- Σ_L → Σ_M, A ↦ supp°_M(A), conjecturally equal to {x ∈ M | omb°(x) ⊂ A}.
He proves the first lands in supports using cosupp°_M(A) = cosupp°_M(omb°A). He starts checking the claimed equality for the second.

This page.
1. He finishes that check. If X ∈ supp°_M(A), then omb°(X) ⊂ supp°_M(A), because the support is formed by intersection (or closed under ∩). So the equality holds: 'OK'.
2. He concludes that the two maps are mutually inverse order isomorphisms Σ_L ⇄ Σ_M, compatible with the complement-type operation 'C'.
3. He notes that this is purely formal and abstracts it:
   - Data: a map o: M → P(L) extending x ↦ {x} on L (a commutative triangle), and a symmetric antireflexive relation ∥_L on L.
   - Induced relation on M: X ∥ Y iff for all x ∈ o(X) and y ∈ o(Y), x ∥_L y.
   - Supports are then the Galois-closed sets of the polarity defined by ∥.
   - A crossed-out attempt defined φ(A) = {X ∈ M | o(X) ⊂ A}; the corrected statement keeps 'two reciprocal isomorphisms Σ_L ⇄ Σ_M'.
4. Special case: if ∥_L is x ≠ y (the 'quasi-ensembliste' case), every subset of L is closed, so Σ_M ≃ P(L).
5. Simplicial case: supp°(A) is identified with omb°(A).
6. Left margin: a further generalisation to a relation between two pairs (M, L) and (M′, L′).

In modern terms, (L, ∥) is an orthogonality space (an irreflexive symmetric relation). Supports are its biorthogonally closed subsets, forming a complete ortholattice. The theorem says that this closure lattice is unchanged when L is enlarged to M with the relation induced through the map o. That is the standard fact that a polarity's concept lattice is determined by a 'join-dense' generating set. The next page explains the motivation: an 'abstract' theory so that 'immersions' can be discussed outside the quasi-set-theoretic case, e.g. for 'cordes'.
errors: No mathematical error is visible. The bijection claim depends on the generic dimensional hypothesis ('Mag L 2') invoked on the previous page; this hypothesis is not restated here.
The sentence 'Il faudrait dire que Γ est type de revêtement général, mais Γ_C réification!' is too unclear to check.

ideas.what: The lattice of (interior) supports on M is isomorphic to that on the subset L via S ↦ S∩L and A ↦ {x | omb°(x) ⊂ A}
ideas.modern_name: Restriction of a closure system / Galois connection to a dense generating subset

ideas.what: Supports defined from a symmetric antireflexive relation ∥ on L and its pullback to M along o: M → P(L)
ideas.modern_name: Orthogonality space; biorthogonal closure; complete ortholattice of orthoclosed sets

ideas.what: When ∥ is the relation ≠, all subsets are closed, so Σ_M ≃ P(L)
ideas.modern_name: Discrete orthogonality space gives a Boolean lattice

ideas.what: Abstract 'support' theory designed to treat immersions and 'cordes' outside the set-theoretic case (Analysis situs programme, tame topology)
ideas.modern_name: Combinatorial or o-minimal stratified spaces (tame topology)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck, Esquisse d'un programme (tame topology programme); van den Dries (o-minimality)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme only sketches tame topology; this support formalism is not there as far as I know

missed.claim: Grothendieck's 'supports' in his 1986 Analysis situs are exactly the orthoclosed sets of an orthogonality space. His Σ_L ≅ Σ_M is the invariance of the closure lattice under a dense extension. This links his combinatorial topology drafts to orthogonality spaces / formal concept analysis, a link nobody seems to have recorded.
missed.quote: C'est formel en termes de ... ∥_L relation symé. antiréfl. sur L ... X ∥ Y ⇔ o(X) ∥ o(Y)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mainly of historical and interpretive interest for editing the Analysis situs manuscripts. The mathematics itself is standard.

missed.claim: He suggests generalising to relations between two systems (M, L) and (M′, L′), i.e. morphisms of such support structures, but does not develop it.
missed.quote: Ou bien généralisation en termes d'une relation ... entre deux ensembles M, M′ avec L, L′
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Hints at a category of support structures relevant to tame or combinatorial stratified spaces. Very sketchy.

deep.surprise_reason: The content is a formal lattice and Galois-connection argument that a specialist would find routine. It is of interest only as part of the unpublished Analysis situs drafts and for its implicit use of orthogonality-space ideas.
transcription_corrections: Line 1: 'X ∈ ensemble W°_U(A)' should probably read 'X ∈ supp°_M(A)'. Likewise 'W°_U(A)' → 'supp°_M(A)' elsewhere.
'ouvs°(X)' and 'ouvs°(A)' are likely 'omb°(X)' and 'omb°(A)' (ombre), consistent with the previous page.
'puisque W° est fermé par ∩' likely means 'puisque supp° est formé par ∩' (or 'fermé par ∩').
'cas quasi-discontinuité' should likely be 'cas quasi-ensembliste' (compare the next page).
'La notion de supp simplicial' probably reads 'La notion de support simplicial : supp° A s'identifie à omb°(A)'.
The relation is ∥, not ⊢. The diagram is L ⊂ M → P(L) with x ↦ {x}, labelled 'comm.', and the restriction map is X ↦ omb°(X).
